analysis: Examined the two head_text excerpts of fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json (lines 12334-13516). They contain only public synthetic prompt-contract/cache-parity vectors: json_schema and long_prompt cases for gemma-4-26b, with request_body, provider_body, template_input, plan (prompt_contract_id, block-boundary chain hashes) and token_ids. The patch excerpt shows other hunks adding an additional_context {enable_thinking:false} member and regenerating token counts and chain hashes. The text is public synthetic data, with no secrets, credentials, keys, real consumer content or executable code. The change is a test fixture and does not alter authorization, attestation, encryption, routing or the App Attest boundaries (TB-002, TB-011). The relevant threat is T-041 (cross-tenant prefix-cache chain hash and timing oracle). The fixture only pins deterministic chain-hash vectors and does not change cache keying or scoping; scope_id is the fixed 'fixture-scope'. The prompt_contract_id in the visible excerpts (7fa068ec...) differs from the one in the patch hunk (8171fec3...), which is plausible for different templates or cases. I could not verify from the supplied evidence that the chain hashes match the real prompt-contract implementation, or that the Swift and Go consumers agree with the new additional_context semantics. Those are consistency and correctness questions, not demonstrated security regressions. The patch excerpt is truncated and the consuming source was not supplied, so cross-file behaviour (how additional_context affects the cache-key contract, whether consumer-controlled additional_context could change the template and alias the cache) is unverified. No finding is raised.
